TokenBatch::offsets¶

Back to TokenBatch API Reference

Signature¶

const Note& TokenBatch::offsets() const

Recover Every Ragged Row Boundary¶

offsets() returns the rank-one Int64 Note that maps the flattened tokens() payload back to logical source cells. If the operation processed N cells, the Note contains N + 1 cumulative boundaries. Cell r owns the half-open token interval [offsets[r], offsets[r + 1]).

The representation maintains four invariants:

  • the Note has NoteDType::Int64 and rank one

  • the first offset is 0

  • offsets are nondecreasing, so every interval is valid

  • the final offset equals tokens().numel() for a present token payload

Adjacent equal values represent an empty source cell. This preserves every row boundary without sentinel strings or padding. The source’s multidimensional shape is not stored in TokenBatch; cells are represented in the source Note’s row-major flat order. Retain the source shape separately if the ragged rows must later be mapped back to coordinates.

For an undefined input propagated through a token-producing operation, the canonical offsets Note is [0] and tokens() is undefined. For a present zero-cell input, offsets is also [0], but tokens() is a defined empty Note. Inspect tokens().defined() to distinguish those states.

The returned const Note& is borrowed from the batch. Access is constant-time and allocates nothing. Copying the returned Note creates a cheap owning handle to the same immutable storage. Calling offsets() on a default-constructed undefined TokenBatch throws pluss::Error.

Example 1: Inspect The Boundary Note¶

const auto batch =
    pluss::note::make({"red green", "", "blue"}).nlp().tokens();
const auto& offsets = batch.offsets();

std::cout << "dtype=" << pluss::dtype_name(offsets.dtype())
          << " shape=[" << offsets.size(0) << "] values=[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets.integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

dtype=Int64 shape=[4] values=[0, 2, 2, 3]

Four boundaries encode three source cells. The repeated 2 marks the empty middle cell.

Example 2: Reconstruct Rows Without Copying¶

const auto batch =
    pluss::note::make({"red green", "", "blue"}).nlp().tokens();
const auto bounds = batch.offsets().integers();

for (std::size_t row = 0; row + 1 < bounds.size(); ++row) {
  std::cout << "row " << row << ": [";
  for (std::int64_t i = bounds[row]; i < bounds[row + 1]; ++i)
    std::cout << (i == bounds[row] ? "" : ", ")
              << '"' << batch.tokens().at(i) << '"';
  std::cout << "]\n";
}

Output¶

row 0: ["red", "green"]
row 1: []
row 2: ["blue"]

Iteration is linear in the number of rows plus tokens. No nested container is materialized.

Example 3: Every Row May Be Empty¶

const auto batch = pluss::note::make({"", "!!!"}).nlp().tokens();
for (const auto value : batch.offsets().integers())
  std::cout << value << ' ';
std::cout << '\n';

Output¶

0 0 0

The final offset is zero because the flat token count is zero, while the three boundaries still preserve two rows.

Example 4: Propagated Absence Uses The Canonical Boundary¶

const auto batch = pluss::Note::undefined().nlp().tokens();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "tokens-defined=" << batch.tokens().defined()
          << " offsets=[" << batch.offsets().integers().front() << "]\n";

Output¶

tokens-defined=false offsets=[0]

Example 5: Undefined Handle Access Is Rejected¶

const pluss::TokenBatch batch;
try {
  (void)batch.offsets();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "default offsets: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

default offsets: rejected

See Also¶

  • tokens: the flat payload indexed by these boundaries.

  • empty: test the final token cardinality in constant time.

  • defined: guard payload access on optional handles.
